newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Only sore knees caused Mandela postpone Asia trip.
newsitem.headline: Only sore knees caused Mandela postpone Asia trip.

text.p: No one doubts that President Nelson Mandela's last-minute postponement of a four-nation trip to South East Asia was because of a sore knee, but diplomats said he was the only person who could get away with it.
Mandela, 78, phoned leaders in the Philippines, Singapore, Malaysia and Brunei at the weekend to say he was cancelling a visit due to start next Saturday.

"He can get away with it because people will forgive him virtually anything, but I cannot think of another world leader who could make so many last-minute changes and not lose credibility," a diplomat told Reuters.
Mandela has cancelled, postponed or cut short several foreign visits since he became the country's first democratically-elected president in April 1994.
Reasons given have included his health, which was undermined by 27 years in apartheid jails, exhaustion, and changed political circumstances in host countries.
The South African department of foreign affairs gave no reason on Monday for the sudden announcement Mandela would not leave for Southeast Asia as planned.
President Fidel Ramos of the Philippines answered the riddle when he said in Manila that Mandela had phoned him personally, citing health reasons for cancelling the visit.
"That's what we are hearing, too," said a Western diplomat in Pretoria.
"Apparently the President's knee has not healed as quickly as his doctors had hoped and he would not be able to cope with the standing and walking of a four-nation trip," he said.
A spokeswoman for Mandela said he was still recovering from a September 14 operation to drain fluid from his right knee.
